answer: Each identity registers a pollination route, locking a 70-credit bond. It collects nectar only from tagged blossoms. Each blossom carries a pearl tag bound to key and epoch, and yields one receipt; reuse is rejected. An auditor recomputes receipts against the ledger, burning the bond on mismatch or outside the comet window. The first route pays 30 credits; the kth pays 30+6(k-1), so the 1000th pays 6024 and 1000 fake identities pay 3,027,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-blossom ring fails, since a claimed blossom yields no second receipt. An honest agent pays 30 and locks 70 once.
